questions.stem: How do guard cells control the opening and closing of stomata?

options.text: They contract like muscle cells to pull the stomata open
They release carbon dioxide which inflates the pore
When guard cells absorb water by osmosis they become turgid and the stoma opens
They produce a waxy cuticle that blocks the pore when closed

questions.explanation: When guard cells take up water by osmosis, they swell and become turgid. Because their inner walls are thicker than their outer walls, they curve apart and the stoma opens. When they lose water, they become flaccid and the stoma closes.
